title: Post-CABG Progressive AV Block — Temporary Pacing Recognition

patient.name: John Alvarez
patient.procedure: POD1 s/p CABGx3 (LIMA-LAD, SVG-OM, SVG-PDA) — epicardial pacing wires placed intraoperatively, atrial and ventricular

stages.label: Baseline — POD1, stable sinus rhythm
stages.facilitatorNotes: Epicardial wires are in place but not connected to a pacer. Nothing abnormal yet — this is the pre-deterioration baseline a learner should compare everything against.

stages.label: Stage II — Emerging 1° AV Block
stages.facilitatorNotes: PR prolongation on the strip. Usually asymptomatic and easy to miss if the learner isn't measuring intervals — a good early prompt: 'has anyone looked at the PR interval today?'

stages.label: Stage III — Progression to Mobitz I (Wenckebach)
stages.facilitatorNotes: Progressively lengthening PR then a dropped beat. This is the point a learner should be escalating — notifying the surgical team and confirming the epicardial wires are readily connectable, not waiting for it to worsen further.

stages.label: Stage IV — Complete Heart Block

successCriteria.label: Correctly identified complete heart block (AV dissociation) on the strip
Connected epicardial wires to the temporary pacer and initiated pacing

stages.facilitatorNotes: Symptomatic bradycardia with a real hemodynamic hit (MAP 63). Watch what the learner actually does here — this stage doesn't auto-advance; move to the branch stage once you've seen enough to judge the response, whether that's fast or slow.

stages.label: Facilitator checkpoint — was pacing initiated appropriately?

branches.label: Learner initiated pacing promptly, capture confirmed
Pacing delayed or capture not achieved

stages.facilitatorNotes: Pick based on what actually happened at the bedside — this isn't timed, it's your call as the facilitator.

stages.label: Paced rhythm — capture confirmed, hemodynamics restored
stages.facilitatorNotes: Effective rhythm now reads 'Paced (VVI)' automatically once captured — the underlying intrinsic conduction problem hasn't gone away, pacing is just overriding it. Good debrief point: what would happen if the learner turned the pacer off right now?

stages.label: Unaddressed — symptomatic bradycardia progressing
stages.facilitatorNotes: Debrief on recognizing the AV block progression EARLY (stages II-III) and having the pacer at bedside ready, rather than reacting only once complete heart block is symptomatic.
